name: genesis-wilds
description: Genesis with a landscape worth crossing. The same speculative physics (docs/speculative-physics.md) and the same two clocks - thirst three times faster than hunger, neither with a remedy - but the ground under them is now six terrains deep: wild grasslands, forest, lake, boggy marsh, open hills, and impassable crag. Every feature sits where it plausibly belongs. Outcrops, flint, and the copper and tin veins break out of the hills, not the grass; a spring rises where the rock does; reeds and clay are marsh things; deadwood, thickets, mushrooms, and the rare bead of tree resin are forest things; brambles want the open edge. Copper and tin are separate veins and neither is worth anything alone. Two kinds of beast graze it and neither will let you close: deer drift, band up, and bolt at four tiles; hares sit still and bolt at five. Nothing here carries a stock and nothing here has a verb. It is a world of nouns, arranged so that where you are stops being the same question as where you stand - which is the whole point, because a physics precipitated out of a flat plain and a physics precipitated out of country are not the same physics. One thing in the ground itself gives: grassland that is walked over often enough wears down into a dirt path, so the routes people actually use surface on the map as lines - the country keeping its own record of habit. Two harmless world clocks cycle underneath it all: time of day turns over roughly every two hundred ticks, time of year roughly every two thousand.

dynamicRules.description: Everyone's satiation drains, slowly - about two thousand ticks from full to starving.
Fires once when someone first becomes starving.

emit.interrupt: you are starving, and nothing in this world feeds you yet - finding or making a way to eat is now your only task

dynamicRules.description: Starving wears the body down slowly - thousands of ticks, not hundreds.
Everyone's hydration drains, three times faster than satiation - about seven hundred ticks from slaked to parched.
Fires once when someone first becomes parched.

emit.interrupt: you are parched, and nothing in this world lets you drink yet - the water is right there and you cannot touch it; finding or making a way to drink is now your only task

dynamicRules.description: Being parched wears the body down twice as fast as starving does.
Fires once when someone's health first drops to a critical level.

emit.interrupt: your health is critical - stop and see to your survival before anything else

dynamicRules.description: At zero health you die: untagged out of the living and left as a corpse.
The map extends north as soon as someone can see that edge.
The map extends east as soon as someone can see that edge.
The map extends south as soon as someone can see that edge.
The map extends west as soon as someone can see that edge.
A deer drifts a tile at a time while it feeds - unhurried, and never while it is standing in the lake.
A deer with no company inside two tiles closes on the nearest of its own - the reason they end up in loose bands rather than scattered singly.

A deer breaks away from anyone inside five tiles - two tiles at a go, but no oftener than every third tick. The cooldown is the whole balance of the thing: a deer that fled every tick could never be reached by anything, and a resource nobody can ever reach is scenery. This one outpaces a walk on open ground and loses that edge to patience, cover, or something thrown.
A hare sits still far more than it moves; when it does move it is one tile and no further.

A hare is the opposite bet to a deer. It backs its stillness and lets you come all the way to arm's reach, then goes three tiles at once. So a hare is easy to walk up on and almost impossible to keep hold of - the reverse of the deer's problem, and it wants a different answer.

Grass that is walked on wears down, a footfall at a time, into a dirt path. Slow enough that one crossing leaves nothing, steady enough that a route used every day becomes visible as a line on the country - the map recording how it is used.
An animal that bolted into the lake founders there until it finds its way back out. The one rule that is allowed to move a beast off water, so nothing can end up stranded mid-lake.
The day turns over, about two hundred ticks from dawn back to dawn.
At the far edge of the day, it wraps back to dawn.

emit.text: night gives way to dawn again

dynamicRules.description: The year turns over, about two thousand ticks from one thaw to the next.
At the far edge of the year, it wraps back to the start of the cycle.

emit.text: the year turns over into another cycle of seasons

bands.serious: You are very hungry - find food soon.
bands.critical: You are starving. Eat now, or getting food is your only task.

bands.serious: You are parched - find water soon.
bands.critical: You are dying of thirst. Drink now, or getting water is your only task.
